primary_question: Do product-specific logistics-network variables improve 3-month-ahead U.S. HS import-price forecasts beyond the same price/macro baseline plus aggregate GSCPI?

models.M0: price history + broad ex-fuel import prices + fuel import prices + seasonality
models.M3: M0 + GSCPI + granular Census network variables

network_feature_families: country and port rerouting/turnover versus 12 months earlier
product exposure to leave-one-product-out port/route flow shocks using pre-test exposure weights
estimation: standardized ridge, tuning restricted to pre-test information; identical forecast origins across models
leakage_rule: At forecast origin, training examples only if their future BLS target is already released/known; Census features are lagged conservatively by publication availability.
uncertainty: 6-month moving-block bootstrap over calendar forecast origins, retaining all product categories together
failure_interpretation: If M3 does not materially and robustly beat M1, the granular-network forecasting premise is not supported at the predeclared commercial-relevance threshold.
important_limitation: Census historical files/API expose current/revised history rather than complete vintage snapshots; retrospective tests remain pseudo-real-time even with conservative release lags. Prospective forecasts must be snapshotted immutably.
